notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-39fac3 (issue #1446). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. The recorded hash matches byte for byte: the open-access published PDF on Centre Mersenne, a07a6143...f13794. Its page tree reports 107 pages, as the extraction records. I also took the arXiv v2 e-print (a nine-file LaTeX project in Latin-1, with a custom entete-hanoi.sty) and used it throughout as a reading aid - which mattered, because two of the findings turn out to be revision artifacts where the preprint is correct and the published text is not.

Numbering and coverage. The numbering is four-level and comes from a custom macro layer: the paragr environment steps the subsubsection counter, so numbered paragraphs run 1.1.1, 1.1.2, ..., and every statement environment (theoreme, proposition, corollaire, lemme, remarque) shares one theo counter reset by subsubsection, giving numbers like 1.1.5.1. local.tex and parts of finalJchi.tex use the abbreviations bpar/epar for the same environment, which a simulation has to count too. Simulating all of that across the eight input files gives 93 numbered statements and 190 numbered paragraphs, and reproduces the extraction's numbers exactly, including Theorems 1.1.5.1, 1.1.5.3 and 1.1.6.1 and the appendix's A.0.x.y form (the appendix has no subsections, so its statements really are printed A.0.9.1, A.0.11.1 and so on - I checked two of them in the published PDF).

Coverage is complete: all 93 statements are covered once the paper's own locator style is respected, since the extraction cites paragraph ranges (§§2.2.1-2.2.13) as well as statement numbers, and a paragraph citation covers the statements inside it.

Internal references. I audited every '<word> \ref{label}' in the source against the environment carrying the label - the audit that found two unrecorded mis-citations in the Groechenig-Wyss-Ziegler review earlier today. Here there are 197 such citations and no mismatch at all, no duplicate labels and no undefined references. This paper is clean in that class.

Statuses. Both library items were read in the Mathlib source at pinned 082e2d3: WithSeminorms.banach_steinhaus and PolynormableSpace.banach_steinhaus with the class BarrelledSpace (Analysis/LocallyConvex/Barrelled.lean:165, :193, :91) and PhragmenLindelof.vertical_strip (Analysis/Complex/PhragmenLindelof.lean:275). The 14 planned items and the routes cite 14 layers between them; all exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. Three Part IIs, one new roadmap and three source routes, all accepted; see the route verdicts. Every non-source route is a joined proposal: each roadmap id, parent and title is shared with at least one other extraction, and in each case the paper that introduced it is identifiable (Zhang 2021 for the Jacquet-Rallis Part II, BPLZZ for the Schwartz-multiplier Part II, Jiang-Zhang for the Gan-Gross-Prasad framework).

Mistakes in the paper. All ten are confirmed, each checked in the published text. Four are settled by the paper against itself: (8.2.3.4) carries eta_{G'} and (8.2.3.5), in the same sentence, eta_{[G']} (E4); section 10.1.5 says 'in the sense of Section 5.1.3' where section 10.2.1 says 'Section 4.3.2' (E7); Proposition 4.3.7.1's limit is over [G'] where the expansion it starts from is over [G']_0 (E3); and Lemma 4.3.6.2 places lambda in ia^G_{P_1} where the proposition above it integrates over the dual space (E9). One is settled by arithmetic: |S_Pi| = 2^{-dim(a_P)} cannot hold for a cardinality, and (10.3.2.1) carries |S_Pi|^{-1} (E5). One by invariance: only (det h)^{-n} gives a translation-invariant top form on GL_n, and the paper's own local measure in section 9.1.2 is that one (E10).

Two are revision artifacts, and the preprint proves it: the published proof of Proposition 10.1.6.1 writes X^h_pi where arXiv v1 writes X^h_0 (E6), and the published section 6.3 writes A_0 in (6.3.0.4)-(6.3.0.5) although it renamed that space to ia*_{M,0}, which is exactly the identification the entry proposes; arXiv v1 defines A and A_0 explicitly (E8). Recording that the preprint is correct in both places is worth doing for anyone reading the two texts side by side.

E1, the one gap, was followed to its source. BPLZZ Theorem 4.14(4) says what the entry says; the proof of 4.14 ends 'For (4) ... follows from Proposition 4.13(1)'; and 4.13 assumes a cuspidal form with non-vanishing period and argues by contradiction from 'weak base change does not exist'. BPLZZ's own Remark 4.15 notes that Theorem 4.14 also follows from Mok and Kaletha-Minguez-Shin-White, which supports the entry's alternative repair and its classification as affecting the proof only. I did not re-derive the step that chi' is CAP when the base change is non-cuspidal.

One amendment in place. E2's reason said the cited BPLZZ numbers 'are those of the first arXiv version'. That is right for sections 3 and 4 - I rebuilt both versions' numbering from source and confirmed th:isolation_tri 3.17 to 3.19, th:abc 4.12 to 4.14 and le:modify 4.10 to 4.12 - but not for the two section 1 citations: th:ggp is 1.8 and th:nonvanishing is 1.9 in v1 and in the Annals text alike, so 'Theorem 1.7' and 'Theorem 1.8' are off by one in every public version. The corrections the entry gives are unaffected; the sentence has been amended to say this.

Verdict: accept.
